maya (support): FYI - multiple customers reporting that calls to /v1/generate are returning 5xx instead of 4xx when they exceed quota. They expect 429 but see 500/502. Customer reported request-id: req_0a1b2c3d and a curl example.

kevin (oncall): which region? any correlating deploys?

maya (support): region: us-west-2. No recent deploys from the customer side. Saw spike around 12:04 UTC. Attaching the curl they used: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-02-28T11:58:12Z to gateway-svc completed for canary=stable (hash a1f3). No other changes in routing configs in the last 24h.

marco (infra): I see a cluster-level surge and a pile of 502s from quota-checker when it tries to contact throttle-cache. Logs: ```[2026-02-28T12:04:05Z] quota-checker -> throttle-cache: dial tcp 10.11.5.23:6379: i/o timeout; overall error: upstream timeout -> returning 502 to gateway``` Looks like dependency timeouts turning into 502s.

lina (eng-runtime): Important note: gateway has a route rule that should map quota failures to 4xx (429) for client-visible errors, but the mapping only applies when the quota-checker responds with a well-formed quota-deny. If quota-checker itself returns an upstream error (502) the gateway currently passes that 502 through. That's a config gap — we should map dependency failures -> 504/503 or canonical 429? we want to avoid exposing 5xx for quota violations.

kevin (oncall): Repro steps requested. maya can you ask a customer to reproduce with headers X-Request-ID and include `x-redwood-auth`? Also need the gateway logs for that request-id.

maya (support): Customer produced logs - here's the slice for req_0a1b2c3d: ```gateway: req_0a1b2c3d received /v1/generate -> forwarded to quota-checker; quota-checker: timeout calling throttle-cache -> error 502; gateway: proxied 502 back to client``` They also attached a stack showing quota-checker blocking awaiting redis-like throttle-cache.

marco (infra): Looking deeper, throttle-cache (redis-variant) in us-west-2 had a transient network partition to the quota-checker pods due to node maintenance. Connection attempts hit the platform-level timeout (1.5s) and the quota-checker doesn't treat timeout as "quota denied" so it bubbles up as 502.

lina (eng-runtime): Short term mitigation options: 1) In gateway routing config add a translation rule: if upstream is quota-checker and response is 5xx -> return 429 with header `x-redwood-internal:quota-fallback` so clients see 4xx; 2) Add a fallback in quota-checker: on dependency timeout return a well-formed deny (429) with reason "quota-unavailable"; 3) Circuit-break throttle-cache so quota-checker can fail fast with a deny instead of 502.

kevin (oncall): Which is lowest risk to ship quickly?

lina (eng-runtime): Gateway mapping (1) is lowest-risk config change and can be patched in <30m. Quota-checker change (2) is code change and needs tests. Circuit-breaker (3) requires infra changes. I'd do (1) as hotfix, then (2) as follow-up.

marco (infra): I've already placed throttle-cache nodes back in service and removed the maintenance fence. I'm watching the connection success rate - it's improving. But traffic that hit during the window will still have gotten 502.

maya (support): Customer wants rollback or immediate fix — they saw 40% of requests return 5xx for ~6 minutes. Can we prioritize the gateway mapping?

lina (eng-runtime): I'm going to push gateway mapping patch to canary now: rule: `if upstream_service=="quota-checker" && status >= 500 && status < 600 -> return 429 with body {"error":"quota_unavailable"}` will also add `x-redwood-incident:throttle-502-mapped` header.

deploy-bot: starting rollout: gateway-config/patch-1794502000 by lina (eng-runtime) -> canary 1/5 at 12:22 UTC.

kevin (oncall): Support script to send to customers while patch lands: "We're investigating - the team deployed a config change to ensure quota failures return 429 instead of 5xx. Please retry requests; idempotent requests are safe. We'll follow up with timeline." Add suggested debug instructions: include `X-Req` header and `--verbose` curl.

maya (support): Sent to customer and asked for logs if they still see 5xx. They responded: a few new requests after 12:24 still showed 502 but most are 429 now. They included new request-id req_0a1b2c9f which returned 429 and body `{"error":"quota_unavailable","retry_after":30}`

lina (eng-runtime): Canary looks good, promoting to 3/5 now. Will complete full rollout if no regressions in 15m. Also filing follow-up ticket to make quota-checker return well-formed denies on dependency timeouts (ENG-RUNTIME-345).

marco (infra): Confirmed throttle-cache health stabilized at 12:31 UTC, connection error rate dropped to near-zero.

kevin (oncall): Incident severity set to SEV3 (customer impact: transient 5xx instead of 429). Owner: eng-runtime. Follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME-345 (deny-on-dep-timeout), INFRA-789 (circuit-breakers for throttle-cache), OPS-logs (improve visibility mapping).

maya (support): Customer updated: most requests now show 429 and they accepted the explanation. Closing customer escalation but keeping incident open until follow-ups are scheduled.

sre-bot: Incident note created: incident/1794502000 - throttle-cache partition caused quota-checker timeouts -> gateway exposed 5xx. Mitigations: gateway mapping hotfix applied, throttle-cache repaired.

lina (eng-runtime): Adding repro steps for the follow-up ticket: 1) run synthetic load against quota-checker while simulating connection timeout to throttle-cache (iptables DROP or simulate high latency) 2) observe quota-checker behavior and gateway response codes 3) implement unit test for timeout->deny translation. Example test curl: ```for i in 1 2 3; do curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-TEST" -H "X-Req: test-$i" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://canary-gateway.internal/v1/generate; done```

kevin (oncall): thanks all. I'll update the incident log and make sure follow-ups are assigned.

maya (support): closing thread for customer comms; will reopen if they see regressions. :thumbsup:
